copy_rules: Write natural business Japanese in です/ます form. No casual forms, no direct translation of English slogans.
Write the product name in Latin letters on screen; give the katakana reading only in narration.
Lead with the buyer's concern and concrete proof before the product claim.
Prefer specific numbers and named sources over superlatives.
Keep each narration line under 45 Japanese characters so it reads in about 5 seconds.
style_rules: Higher information density than a US page: headline plus two or three short supporting points per scene.
Show proof on screen: source names, numbers, customer or partner names when sourced.
Use the brand's own colors; set Japanese text in Noto Sans JP, bold for headlines.
Calm, precise motion. No slang, no exaggerated effects.

questions.q: Is the tone appropriate for a Japanese enterprise buyer?
Are security, data location or support concerns addressed with evidence?
Is there local proof such as Japanese customers, partners, pricing in yen or local sources?
Is it clear what the product does and what to do next?
